cards.b: Records the income of a business and all costs to earn it over a period of time (e.g. a year).
Profit left after tax and dividends, kept in the business as a source of finance.
Shows the value of assets and liabilities at one point in time (a snapshot).
Current: turned into cash within a year (inventories, receivables, cash). Non-current: kept for more than a year (buildings, machinery).
Current: due within a year (trade payables, overdraft). Non-current: repayable after more than a year (long-term loan).
Shareholders' equity + non-current liabilities. Total long-term finance invested in the business.
Profit ÷ capital employed × 100. Compare with the interest rate a bank would pay.
Current assets ÷ current liabilities. Around 1.5–2 is usually acceptable. It is a number such as 2:1, not a %.
(Current assets − inventories) ÷ current liabilities. Around 1 is acceptable. Stricter than the current ratio.
Profitability: ability to generate profit. Liquidity: ability to pay short-term debts. A profitable firm can still lack liquidity.
Based on past data; do not explain why; inflation and different accounting methods distort; ignore non-financial factors.

short.q: Calculate the gross profit margin for revenue of $400,000 and cost of sales of $280,000. [2]
Calculate ROCE for profit of $45,000 and capital employed of $300,000. [2]
Current assets are $90,000, inventories $30,000 and current liabilities $60,000. Calculate the current ratio and the acid test ratio. [3]
Explain the difference between profitability and liquidity. [3]
short.model: Profitability is the ability to make profit from revenue or capital. Liquidity is the ability to pay short-term debts, so a profitable business may still fail if it lacks liquid funds.
points: liquidity: ability to pay short-term debts

short.q: A business's revenue rose 12% but its profit margin fell from 12% to 7.5%. Explain two possible reasons. [4]
short.model: Cost of sales may have risen faster than revenue, for example through dearer materials. Expenses such as rent or wages may also have risen.
